Use Tier 2: model_design, with corresponding training_evaluation and predictor updates, to add a gated history-pooling layer inside SASRec. The latest trial reached macro HR@10 of 0.4463 versus the 0.505 baseline, with particularly large declines in CDs_and_Vinyl and Movies_and_TV. A testable hypothesis is that scoring from only the final sequence representation inadequately preserves persistent preferences in these categories; the aggregate results do not establish this cause.

For each sequence position, compute the cumulative mean of preceding and current nonpadding item embeddings, then project this history summary into the SASRec feature space. Learn a vector gate from the contextual feature and projected summary, and fuse them into one representation before the existing tied-embedding scoring layer. Compute pooling causally at every supervised position so earlier training targets cannot access later interactions. Train the pooling projection, gate, encoder, item embeddings, and existing item bias jointly under the current sampled cross-entropy objective. Keep sampling, optimizer, dimensions, seeds, and training limits unchanged to isolate this architectural change.

Save exactly one selected checkpoint per category and update the predictor writer to reconstruct the same fused architecture with identical history truncation and padding. Select checkpoints using validation HR@10 with 200 users, 99 unique negatives, and evaluation seed 42, and report the four-category macro-average while leaving the pinned host evaluator authoritative. Preserve DATA_DIR, all four routes, and existing splits; do not access test labels or generate a test submission during search.
